Reviewed latest TTFT and p95 numbers from last week's benchmarks, discussed enabling streaming to improve TTFT, and explored kernel/quantization trades (flash-attn vs fused kernels). Identified next steps: run streaming-enabled benchmarks at seq_len 128 and 512, try 4-bit quant + flash-attn kernel, and produce updated latency spreadsheet for NovaPay. Action owners assigned.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Liu (Redwood SRE), Elena Ortiz (NovaPay), Samir Patel (NovaPay Infra), Tom Nguyen (NovaPay PM)

00:00 Jordan: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync for latency tuning, um Jordan from Redwood, Priya and Marco are with me. Elena: hey thanks, appreciate it.
00:22 Priya: quick agenda - run through last week's benchmark numbers, dig into TTFT and streaming impact, look at seq_len variations, then kernel / quantization experiments and then agree next steps. sound good?
00:35 Elena: yup that's perfect.
00:50 Samir: just a note, we had one infra change this morning - our staging cluster bumped to cuda 12.3 on the dedicated nodes, not sure if that will change perf.
01:05 Marco: noted, that can affect some kernels, good to know. we'll flag it when we run the bench.
01:22 Priya: ok numbers first - last week we ran the baseline hosted config with gpt-style model (open-llm-7b-ish) at seq_len 256, no streaming, batch size 1. TTFT p50 was 320 ms, p95 560 ms, p99 1.2 s. throughput token/sec was ~420 tps at steady state.
01:48 Elena: those align with what we saw; p95 is the one our end users worry about. our SLA target for interactive experiences is p95 < 450 ms.
02:05 Jordan: right, so two levers we think will help: enabling streaming to push tokens earlier (improve TTFT) and switching kernels / quant profiles to reduce per-token compute.
02:22 Tom: when you say streaming, do you mean chunked output streaming or chunked decoding? clarify.
02:36 Priya: yeah good question - streaming here = flush-first-token as soon as logits available, we also investigate micro-batching overlap so next token compute and network push overlap. it's not chunking the prompt, it's emit-first-token earlier.
02:58 Samir: any network assumptions? our peering adds ~30 ms RTT to Redwood region.
03:12 Marco: we included a 30-35 ms network RTT in the bench; results earlier included that. so TTFT improvements from streaming are still meaningful.
03:30 Priya: next, we tried enabling FlashAttention-style kernel (note: transcript sometimes says flash a tenshun) with 8-bit quant - that dropped p50 to 260 ms, p95 to 480 ms, p99 to 1.0 s. improvement but p95 still borderline.
03:58 Elena: ok so improvement but not enough. what about seq_len tuning? our median prompt length is closer to 90 tokens but we sized tests at 256.
04:15 Jordan: good point - if you give us the token distribution we can run more representative runs. short seq_len tends to help TTFT a lot because KV cache ops shrink.
04:30 Priya: we ran a quick seq_len 128 run (no streaming) and saw p50 240 ms, p95 420 ms - that actually gets close to NovaPay target. with streaming on top that should pull p95 below 400 ms.
04:52 Samir: so priority is to do streaming + seq_len 128 test.
05:05 Priya: yes. separate discussion - kernel selection. our infra shows two promising paths: (1) FlashAttention fused kernels with 4-bit quant (we saw best per-token cost), (2) optimized cutlass/fused matmul kernels (sometimes labelled cutlass-ep) that are more stable on older CUDA stacks. flash-attn gives lower latency but can be sensitive to cuda driver/arch.
05:38 Marco: also keep in mind our staging is on cuda 12.3, some flash-attn builds require patched libraries; if driver mismatch we might see regressions. cutlass path is more robust.
05:55 Elena: risks - we can't have flakey nodes in production. better to pick the slightly slower stable kernel if variance is a problem.
06:10 Priya: Agreed. our recommendation: run A/B bench across both kernels with 4-bit and 8-bit quant profiles, measure p50/p95/p99 and variance, and then pick stable profile for pilot.
06:28 Tom: about quant - is 4-bit going to affect quality? our product team cares about hallucination and response fidelity.
06:40 Priya: yes there's a measurable quality delta. in our internal evals 4-bit had small differences on long-form completions; for short interactive responses it's often acceptable. we can run your prompt set through both to quantify ROUGE / BLEU-like diffs and a small human eval.
07:00 Elena: we'll share the prompt set, yes.
07:12 Jordan: streaming implementation note - Redwood hosted API supports streaming via SSE and chunked HTTP; for Dedicated we can enable streaming but need to ensure the LB and node config allow flush. Marco can help validate configs.
07:30 Marco: I'll look at keepalive and proxy buffering, we had one customer where Nginx buffering added 200 ms if not tuned.
07:40 Samir: we use Envoy in front, will check buffering flags.
07:48 Priya: next, batching and concurrency - we saw that increasing concurrency beyond 4 increases throughput but harms TTFT for single requests; Redwood Optimize suggested micro-batching policy to prioritize low-latency requests with small batch windows.
08:05 Tom: is there a setting to favor TTFT for interactive routes only? we want background inference to use full batching but interactive to be low-latency.
08:18 Priya: yes, per-route SLO/routing policy. we can pin interactive routes to low-latency pool or set max batch wait to sub-5ms.
08:30 Elena: cost implications? will dedicated pools cost more for pinned low-latency?
08:36 Jordan: reserved low-latency capacity is slightly higher per-token but you save on user experience and avoid tail latency. Redwood pricing model for Dedicated reflects reserved capacity; we can model unit economics in the sheet.
08:50 Priya: back to bench results - we propose this experimental matrix: seq_len {128,512}, streaming {on,off}, kernel {flash-attn-4bit, flash-attn-8bit, cutlass-8bit}, batch_size 1, concurrency 1..4. measure p50/p95/p99 and variance, and record quality metrics on your prompt set.
09:18 Elena: timeline?
09:22 Priya: we can run the full matrix in our infra if you provide prompt set and traffic profile; expect results in 48 hours.
09:32 Samir: what about infra constraints - VPC peering, firewall? we need to coordinate with security.
09:40 Marco: we'll need a short window for ports and peering; I can share a checklist.
09:48 Elena: good. also, mention of audit logs and retention - for pilot we need logs for debugging but must ensure data residency.
10:00 Jordan: Redwood Private can be used for on-prem or VPC mode with customer-managed KMS for encryption. For this trial we can use dedicated instance with logs disabled by default or anonymized.
10:18 Tom: perfect. any blockers?
10:22 Priya: the only technical blocker is verifying flash-attn builds on your cuda 12.3 nodes; if we see incompatibility we'll use cutlass path.
10:32 Samir: we'll provide node images and we can run a quick smoke test.
10:38 Priya: Great. Recap of decisions: 1) Priority experiment is streaming + seq_len 128; 2) Run A/B kernels (flash-attn 4-bit vs cutlass 8-bit) to evaluate latency and variance; 3) Measure quality on NovaPay prompt set; 4) Redwood to deliver updated latency spreadsheet and recommendations by 2026-08-20.
10:58 Elena: sounds good.
11:05 Jordan: we'll also include a note about network RTT assumptions used in bench (we used 30 ms by default). please confirm if your peering RTT differs.
11:18 Samir: will confirm.
11:25 Tom: can we also get a short doc about streaming implementation and required LB flags? Marco?
11:33 Marco: yes I'll draft a checklist and send by 2026-08-21.
11:40 Jordan: ok any other questions?
11:45 Elena: none from me. thanks team.
11:50 Jordan: thanks all. we'll follow up with results and a calendar invite for infra deep dive.
12:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional mis-hearings (flash-attn rendered as flash a tenshun), and speaker labels may shift early in recording. This transcript retains filler and interruptions to reflect authentic meeting flow.
